The drift specification and the attainability of the 31st-year timing option remain the source of the split.

Price specification.
* A is “constant growth rate of 10% each year … the stock price is completely linear with no noise.” Literally that is an arithmetic level line P^A_t = P0[1+0.10 t] a.s., the σ≡0 degenerate case. The finance shorthand reading is P^A_t = P0 1.10^t a.s.
* B is “linear growth trend of 10% each year (i.e., could be modeled by a non-seasonal ARIMA model with drift)”. ARIMA with drift is additive in levels ΔP^B_t = μ+ε_t, E[ε_t|F_{t-}]=0, μ=0.10P0 yr⁻¹. Hence E[P^B_t|F0]=P0+μt=P0[1+0.10t] and E[P^B_{t+Δ}|F_t]=P^B_t+μΔ. After removing the known arithmetic drift the innovations are stationary zero-mean with constant long-run autocovariance. In levels both baskets are sub-martingales with a 10% arithmetic drift; discounted by the deterministic drift they are martingales.

Adapted liquidation on [30,31].
For an F-adapted programme s_t≥0, ∫s_t dt=1, or an adapted stopping time τ∈[30,31],
E[∫ s_t P^B_t dt]=∫ s_t E[P^B_t]dt and E[∫ s_t M_t dt]=0 for the zero-mean martingale part M_t. 
E[P^B_τ]=E[P^B_30]+μE[τ-30] ≤ E[P^B_31] with equality only for τ≡31 a.s. Hence linearity of expectation kills any in-expectation mean premium from timing; the zero-mean 20% weekly shocks contribute zero to the unconditional mean of every causal schedule. The ex-post pathwise supremum M31=sup_{[30,31]}P^B_t satisfies E[M31]>E[P^B_31] and M31≥P^B_30 a.s., but M31 is not an adapted payoff. A causal sell-on-up-move rule forfeits remaining positive drift and cannot realise E[M31] ex ante.

The 31st-year window changes dispersion only, not the unconditional mean. The equal-mean content is captured by C, although “both options are martingales in levels” is sloppy; levels are sub-martingales, drift discounted returns are martingales. The mixed additive-vs-exponential reading P^A_t=P01.10^t a.s. vs E[P^B_t]=P0[1+0.10t] gives strict in-expectation dominance A > B, with dominance in expectation only.

Whether “completely linear with no noise” forces an arithmetic level trend for A and whether the question intends the conventional multiplicative finance drift. Whether the supremum/look-back premium is realisable as an increase in unconditional mean under linear utility with adapted liquidation; mathematics says no mean premium for adapted policies, only a dispersion/realisation effect.

whereas B is the ARIMA-with-drift additive case 
E[P^B_t]=P0[1+0.10t].
Then on any calendar date 
E[P^B_t]=P0[1+0.10t] < P0 1.10^t =P^A_t , t>0,
e.g. E[P^B_30]=4.0P0 ≪ P^A_30≈17.45P0. Linearity of expectation kills any mean premium from an adapted liquidation programme; the mean-maximising adapted rule is τ≡31. The high variance of B is pure risk around a linear mean that is dominated in expectation by the deterministic exponential path of A. The dominance is in expectation only: σ>0 allows a realised B path to finish above the deterministic A payoff, so E and H are false, B,C,D,F are false in levels, and G is not attainable in the adapted sense. The strongest true ordering on this literal ARIMA-additive vs compound-A reading is 
A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than that of choosing basket B.

Unresolved is whether “stock price is completely linear with no noise’’ for A means arithmetic linear P0[1+0.10t] a.s. or deterministic exponential P0 1.10^t a.s., and whether “liquidate … with whatever liquidation strategy will maximise value’’ is interpreted as the ex-ante expectation of an F-adapted policy, which cannot realise the ex-post supremum, or as the ex-post supremum itself, which gives the volatility timing premium. The semantic drift choice drives A vs C vs G. The realised dominance statements E and H are false in all readings because σ>0 allows both directions. The martingale statements B,C,D,F are false in levels because of the 10% drift; they hold only after drift discounting. The dispute is still the level vs log / additive vs multiplicative reading of the 10% and the meaning of “price is completely linear’’.

* Literal additive/level reading that the wording invites
  * A: “price is completely linear with no noise’’ → P_t^A = P0 + μ_a t = P0[1+0.10 t] a.s. with μ_a=0.10 P0 yr⁻¹.
  * B: “linear growth trend … ARIMA with drift’’ → ΔP_t^B = μ_a + ε_t, E[ε_t|F]=0, so P_t^B = P0 + μ_a t + M_t with E[M_t]=0. The 20% weekly moves are stationary zero-mean innovations with constant long-run autocovariance.
  * After removing the known deterministic arithmetic drift the innovations are stationary and drift-adjusted prices \tilde P_t = P_t – μ_a t are zero-mean martingales. In levels both prices are strictly positive sub-martingales with the same 10% arithmetic drift.
  * For an F-adapted liquidation density s_t≥0, ∫_{30}^{31}s_t dt=1, or an adapted stopping time τ∈[30,31],
  E[∫ s_t P_t^B dt]=∫ s_t E[P_t^B]dt and E[∫ s_t M_t dt]=0,
  E[P_τ^B]=E[P_30^B]+μ_a E[τ-30] ≤ E[P_31^B] with equality only for τ≡31 a.s.
  Linearity of expectation kills an ex-ante mean premium from timing. E[sup_{[30,31]}P_t^B]>E[P_31^B] is true for the non-adapted ex-post supremum but the supremum is not an attainable adapted payoff; a causal sell-on-up-move rule forfeits remaining positive drift.
  * Hence on the literal linear-in-levels reading E[P_t^A]=E[P_t^B]=P0[1+0.10 t] on any calendar date and for any admissible causal liquidation programme 
  E[V^A_liq]=E[V^B_liq]=∫_{30}^{31}s_t P0[1+0.10 t]dt,
  maximised in mean by essentially terminal liquidation. The high variance of B is pure risk around the common arithmetic mean.

* Conventional multiplicative finance reading
  * A is read as P_t^A = P0 1.10^t a.s. ; B is read as E[P_{t+dt}|F_t]=P_t 1.10^{dt}. Then E[P_t]=P0 1.10^t on a fixed date for both baskets.
  * With an American/look-back timing privilege in the 31st year 
  E[sup_{[30,31]}P_t^B] > E[P_31^B]=P0 1.10^{31}=E[V^A].
  An adapted gradual liquidation can approach the running maximum and gives the familiar volatility/option premium
  E[V^B_opt] ≥ E[sup_{[30,31]}P_t^B] > E[V^A].
  The premium is in expectation only; realisations of B can lie below the deterministic A payoff, so E and H are false.

Current round: a large block of colleagues keeps the compound A / additive B reading and obtains strict in-expectation dominance of the deterministic compound basket,
A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than that of choosing basket B,
e.g. E[P^B_30]=4.0P0 ≪ P^A_30≈17.45P0. That reading treats “constant growth rate’’ as proportional for A while keeping the explicit ARIMA-with-drift additive specification for B.

A second block keeps the fully linear-in-levels reading P^A_t=P0[1+0.10 t] a.s. and obtains equal unconditional means, the content usually quoted as
C. Since the return distribution is stationary, both options are martingales and so they must have the same expected value,
understood in the drift-adjusted sense. The level-martingale statements B,D,F are false in levels; the processes are sub-martingales with 10% arithmetic drift.

The G camp, 
G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than that of choosing basket A,
is the conventional multiplicative-drift / ex-post-supremum reading: same drifted mean on a fixed date, 31st-year American timing gives E[V^B_opt] > E[V^A] in expectation only.

The phrase “price is completely linear with no noise’’ points to the arithmetic linear reading for A, making the additive reading internally consistent and giving mean equality, i.e. the C content. The “constant growth rate’’ phrasing and the explicit liquidation-maximisation wording point to the conventional proportional-drift / timing-option reading that yields the G premium. 

On the literal linear-in-levels wording forced by “price is completely linear’’ for A and “ARIMA with drift’’ for B, the unconditional means coincide and the 31st-year window changes dispersion only. That is the equal-mean / stationary-return content captured by C on the list, with the usual caveat that the level processes are sub-martingales, not physical martingales, and the dominance is expectation only.
